app.setup.title_default.why: Terse ContentUnavailableView title, Apple's own verb for extensions in Safari; Sie-register held throughout.

app.setup.title_failed.why: Hedged, distinct from the plain not-yet-on title above; does not claim the extension is off.

app.setup.detail_default.s: Geschützte Websites können Ihre Klicks nicht mehr umleiten.
app.setup.detail_default.back: Protected websites can no longer redirect your clicks.
app.setup.detail_default.why: One-sentence payoff, plain declarative, well under the character budget.

app.setup.detail_failed.s: Safari antwortete nicht. Wird die Erweiterung aktiviert, erkennt Undirect das von selbst.
app.setup.detail_failed.back: Safari did not respond. If the extension is activated, Undirect notices that by itself.
app.setup.detail_failed.why: Two clauses joined by a real subordinate construction, not a dash; no raw error code, reassures.

app.setup.open_button.why: Noun-plus-infinitive button style like System Settings; uses Apple's own term 'Erweiterungen'.

app.welcome.heading.why: Matches Apple's own onboarding pattern 'Willkommen bei X'; the one warmer register allowed.

app.welcome.feature.invisible_layers.tit.why: Concrete two-word noun phrase naming the trick, no marketing language.

app.welcome.feature.invisible_layers.det.s: Eine unsichtbare Ebene liegt über der Seite und fängt den Klick ab.
app.welcome.feature.invisible_layers.det.back: An invisible layer lies over the page and intercepts the click.
app.welcome.feature.invisible_layers.det.why: Describes what the person would see, not the mechanism; fits the sentence budget.

app.welcome.feature.swapped_links.title.why: Two-word noun phrase matching the sibling feature headlines.

app.welcome.feature.swapped_links.detail.s: Manche Seiten tauschen das Linkziel im Moment des Klicks aus.
app.welcome.feature.swapped_links.detail.back: Some pages swap the link target in the moment of the click.
app.welcome.feature.swapped_links.detail.why: Plain, concrete, names the timing without technical jargon.

app.welcome.feature.uninvited_windows.ti.why: Direct two-word noun phrase, consistent register with the other feature titles.

app.welcome.feature.uninvited_windows.de.s: Ein neuer Tab öffnet nur das Ziel, das Sie tatsächlich angeklickt haben.
app.welcome.feature.uninvited_windows.de.back: A new tab opens only the destination that you actually clicked.
app.welcome.feature.uninvited_windows.de.why: Written as a promise per the brief; comma-plus-relative-clause instead of a dash.

app.welcome.feature.every_destination.ti.why: Three-word headline naming the rule-list feature, uses vocabulary term 'Ziel'.

app.welcome.feature.every_destination.de.s: Jedes Ziel wird aufgeführt, und Sie entscheiden: hier oder überall.
app.welcome.feature.every_destination.de.back: Every destination gets listed, and you decide: here or everywhere.
app.welcome.feature.every_destination.de.why: Conjunction 'und' carries the clause instead of a dash; keeps both the listing and the scope choice within budget.

app.welcome.feature.one_site_at_a_time.t.why: Two-word verb phrase naming the per-site activation mechanism.

app.welcome.feature.one_site_at_a_time.d.s: Ein Tipp auf das Undirect-Symbol schaltet den Schutz für diese Website ein.
app.welcome.feature.one_site_at_a_time.d.back: One tap on the Undirect icon switches protection on for this site.
app.welcome.feature.one_site_at_a_time.d.why: Names the concrete mechanism (icon, tap) at the edge of the character budget.

app.nav.guarded_sites.why: Direct vocabulary term for guarded/watched sites, works as sidebar label and nav title.

app.nav.settings.why: Apple's own standard German term for this screen on both platforms.

app.nav.app_title.why: Proper noun, left untranslated as instructed.

app.rules.grouping.everywhere.why: One-word scope term, reused consistently for the 'everywhere' concept throughout.

app.rules.grouping.by_site.why: Two-word contrast to 'Überall', reads clearly as the opposing filter.

app.rules.empty_no_app.title.back: No connection to the extension yet
app.rules.empty_no_app.title.why: Names the first-contact/wiring state, distinct from the empty-list state below.

app.rules.empty_no_app.detail.s: Öffnen Sie einmal eine Seite in Safari.
app.rules.empty_no_app.detail.back: Open a page in Safari once.
app.rules.empty_no_app.detail.why: One plain instruction, kept well under the tight character budget.

app.rules.empty_no_rules.title.why: Short content-empty state, contrasts with the wiring state above.

app.rules.empty_no_rules.detail.s: Eine Regel entsteht erst, wenn Sie entscheiden.
app.rules.empty_no_rules.detail.back: A rule appears only once you decide.
app.rules.empty_no_rules.detail.why: States the mechanism (a decision creates the rule) plainly, within budget.

app.rules.footer.lifetime_count.why: Uses 'gestoppt' for attempts stopped, kept distinct from the rule-verdict word 'blockiert'.

app.rules.row.state_blocked.why: Predicate-adjective state word, pairs with 'Zugelassen' below.

app.rules.row.state_allowed.why: Apple's own Screen Time term for 'allow' as a state, held consistently across the whole file.

app.rules.row.action_allow.why: Imperative-infinitive menu-item verb, contrasts with the noun/state form 'Zugelassen'.

app.rules.row.action_block.why: Verb form pairs with 'Zulassen' as the action opposite.

app.rules.row.help_tooltip.why: Terse hover tooltip, within the 30-40 character budget.

app.rules.row.use_default.why: Names clearing the rule back to the default policy, distinct from the Allow/Block verbs.

app.watched.empty.title.why: Plain factual empty-state title within the 3-5 word budget.

app.watched.empty.detail.s: Klicken Sie auf das Undirect-Symbol in Safari, um die Website zu schützen.
app.watched.empty.detail.back: Click the Undirect icon in Safari to protect the site.
app.watched.empty.detail.why: Concrete instruction naming the icon and Safari, trimmed to fit the character budget.

app.watched.footer.s: Neue Websites fügen Sie über Safaris Symbolleiste hinzu.
app.watched.footer.back: You add new sites via Safari's toolbar.
app.watched.footer.why: States the only add-path plainly, within the sentence budget.

app.watched.row.guarded_badge.why: Matches the guard/protect vocabulary root used throughout the app.

app.watched.row.stop_button.why: Apple's standard word for removing a row from an editable list, matching what the button does.

app.watched.row.stop_tooltip.s: Schaltet den Schutz für die Website aus.
app.watched.row.stop_tooltip.back: Switches protection off for the site.
app.watched.row.stop_tooltip.why: Mirrors the button's action, within the 30-40 character budget.

app.settings.guard_toggle.why: One-word noun root for the master switch, reused consistently as the 'guard' concept elsewhere.

app.settings.state_on.why: Apple's own standard toggle-state word in German System Settings.

app.settings.mode_heading.why: Names the run-mode choice directly, within the 3-5 word budget.

app.settings.mode_watched.why: Phrased from the person's own point of view, as the brief asks, within the 3-word budget.

app.settings.mode_everywhere.why: Two words, contrasts cleanly with the mode above, reuses the 'überall' scope term.

app.settings.banner_toggle.why: Compact toggle label naming the page-note concept, within the 3-word budget.

app.settings.policy_heading.why: Names the default-policy concept with one consistent term, 'Standardregel'.

app.settings.policy_block.why: Adverb-plus-verb picker option, pairs with the allow option below.

app.settings.policy_allow.why: Same adverb structure as the block option, uses the consistent verb 'zulassen'.

ext.meta.description.s: Verhindert, dass Websites Ihre Klicks kapern und Sie ungewollt umleiten.
ext.meta.description.back: Prevents websites from hijacking your clicks and redirecting you unintentionally.
ext.meta.description.why: Slightly more explanatory register for a first-time reader in the Extensions list or App Store.

ext.meta.app_title.why: Fallback display name is the product's own name.

ext.toolbar.tooltip_on.why: States the current on-state plainly, within the 4-6 word budget.

ext.toolbar.tooltip_off.why: Comma instead of a dash; doubles as the call to action the tooltip is meant to carry.

ext.toolbar.tooltip_no_site.why: Brief, explains there is nothing here to guard, within the 3-5 word budget.

ext.popup.no_site_title.why: Concise popup headline for the no-website empty state.

ext.popup.no_site_body.s: Öffnen Sie eine Website, dann hier antippen.
ext.popup.no_site_body.back: Open a website, then tap here.
ext.popup.no_site_body.why: Keeps 'hier' as a self-reference to the button the popup hangs off, per the brief's note.

ext.popup.watch_switch_label.s: Schutz für diese Website ein- oder ausschalten
ext.popup.watch_switch_label.back: Switch protection for this site on or off
ext.popup.watch_switch_label.why: Screen-reader-only label spells out the switch's function fully, since no visual context is available.

ext.popup.watch_unknown.s: Hier gibt es nichts zu schützen.
ext.popup.watch_unknown.back: There is nothing to protect here.
ext.popup.watch_unknown.why: Brief reason for the disabled switch, within the 25-35 character budget.

ext.popup.watch_everywhere_mode.why: Explains the switch is redundant, reuses the 'überall' scope term.

ext.popup.watch_master_off.why: Attributes the disabled state to the master switch, not the site, within budget.

ext.popup.watch_on.s: Schutz ist an. Ausschalten lädt die Seite neu.
ext.popup.watch_on.back: Protection is on. Turning it off reloads the page.
ext.popup.watch_on.why: State plus warning as two short clauses, no dash, within the 35-50 character budget.

ext.popup.watch_off.s: Schutz ist aus. Einschalten lädt die Seite neu.
ext.popup.watch_off.back: Protection is off. Turning it on reloads the page.
ext.popup.watch_off.why: Mirrors watch_on's exact sentence shape, as the brief asks for the before/after pair.

ext.popup.page_heading.why: Two-word heading, matches the 'page' vs 'site' vocabulary distinction.

ext.popup.page_off.s: Für diese Seite wird nichts erfasst.
ext.popup.page_off.back: Nothing is being recorded for this page.
ext.popup.page_off.why: Dead key as of 2026-09-22; written speculatively in the same voice as the sibling states.

ext.popup.page_quiet.back: This page has been unremarkable so far.
ext.popup.page_quiet.why: Plain, calm statement that nothing has happened yet, within the 35-45 character budget.

ext.popup.page_empty.s: Hier gibt es noch nichts zu sehen.
ext.popup.page_empty.back: There is nothing to see here yet.
ext.popup.page_empty.why: Dead key, near-synonym of page_quiet as the brief notes; not given distinct effort.

ext.popup.stopped_one.why: Terse badge using 'gestoppt' for the blocked-attempts count, distinct from the rule-verdict word.

ext.popup.stopped_other.why: German predicate adjective is invariant by number in this badge context; same text serves both forms correctly.

ext.popup.seen_one.why: Singular noun 'Versuch' for the broader seen-count, distinct from 'stopped'.

ext.popup.seen_other.why: Correct German plural of 'Versuch', pairs with the singular form above.

ext.popup.tries_one.why: Terse per-destination fragment; German 'Mal' does not inflect for count.

ext.popup.tries_other.why: Same invariant form as the singular, which is correct German for this word.

ext.popup.recipe_heading.why: One-word prefix that reads naturally before the colon and the fix's own name.

ext.state.blocked.why: Consistent with the app-side state word for the same concept.

ext.state.allowed.why: Consistent with the app-side 'Zugelassen', Apple's own Screen Time term.

ext.state.removed.why: Distinct third state word for a local trap with no destination to rule on.

ext.scope.here.why: Composes naturally after a predicate verdict word, e.g. 'Blockiert auf dieser Website'.

ext.scope.everywhere.why: Single adverb composes directly after the verdict word, e.g. 'Blockiert überall'.

ext.scope.default.why: Single adverb, consistent with the 'standardmäßig' used in the settings picker options.

ext.action.allow_here.why: Two-word menu option combining scope and the consistent verb 'zulassen'.

ext.action.allow_everywhere.why: Parallel structure to 'Hier zulassen', reuses the 'überall' scope term.

ext.action.block_here.why: Parallel structure with the allow options above.

ext.action.block_everywhere.why: Parallel structure, completes the four-option menu set.

ext.popup.policy_heading.why: Identical wording to the app-side counterpart, per the brief's note that they should read the same.

ext.policy.block.why: Consistent phrasing with the app-side equivalent option.

ext.policy.allow.why: Consistent phrasing with the app-side equivalent option.

ext.popup.bridge_warning.s: Diese Seite blockiert einen Teil des Schutzes, nicht Undirect selbst.
ext.popup.bridge_warning.back: This page blocks part of the protection, not Undirect itself.
ext.popup.bridge_warning.why: Names the page's own responsibility without CSP jargon, reassures it is not a bug, within budget.

ext.kind.click_catcher.why: Compact compound noun matching the terse comma-joined tag list.

ext.kind.overlay.why: Broader than the click-catcher tag, names any see-through overlay.

ext.kind.synthetic_click.why: Names a script-dispatched click distinctly from a real press.

ext.kind.window_open.why: Standard German compound, one tag, within the 2-word budget.

ext.kind.href_swap.back: Link target swapped during the click
ext.kind.href_swap.why: Names the timing-based trick within the 3-4 word budget.

ext.kind.back_hijack.why: Names the back-gesture hijack distinctly from the plain redirect tag.

ext.kind.redirect.why: Names the core same-tab redirect trick, distinct from back_hijack and pop_tab.

ext.kind.pop_tab.why: Names the tab-under mechanism distinctly from a plain pop-up window.

ext.kind.network_rule.why: Uses 'gestoppt' to tie into the attempt vocabulary, names the earliest block point.

ext.reason.way_back.back: Leads back to the starting page.
ext.reason.way_back.why: Brief reason fragment within the 30-40 character budget.

ext.reason.sized.why: Concise reason within the 25-35 character budget.

ext.reason.took_press.why: Extremely terse to fit the 15-25 character budget; uses 'kapern', the same verb as the extension's own description.

ext.reason.default_allow.why: Terse, ties to the 'Regel' vocabulary term, within the 15-25 character budget.

ext.reason.own_code.why: Concise reason within the 25-35 character budget.

ext.popup.rules_link.why: One word, matches the 'Regel' vocabulary term, plural for the list screen.

ext.popup.back_link.why: Names the popup's main per-page view for a screen reader user with no visual context.

ext.rules.everywhere_heading.why: Consistent with the app-side grouping term.

ext.rules.by_site_heading.why: Consistent with the app-side grouping term.

ext.rules.empty.why: Consistent terse placeholder, matching the app-side wording.

ext.action.allow.why: Same verb as elsewhere, scope already fixed by the section the row is in.

ext.action.block.why: Same verb as elsewhere, pairs with the allow option above.

ext.action.clear.why: Same phrasing as the app-side 'use_default' action, so it reads as the same action across surfaces.

ext.popup.settings_heading.why: Matches Apple's standard term, consistent with the container app's own Settings screen.

ext.settings.guard_label.why: Consistent with the app-side term for the same master switch.

ext.settings.guard_on.why: Matches the standard Apple toggle-state word used consistently across the app.

ext.settings.mode_heading.why: Consistent phrasing with the app-side equivalent heading.

ext.settings.mode_watched.why: Consistent with the app-side mode option.

ext.settings.mode_everywhere.why: Consistent with the app-side mode option.

ext.settings.banner_toggle.why: Tighter 2-word budget than the app-side toggle, keeps the recognizable 'Hinweis' vocabulary term.

ext.action.report.why: Concise two-word action label naming the external report action.
